stem:
Harsh watches white clouds form over the hills near his school after a cool morning, and later sees rain falling on the playground.

Which statement best describes how water vapour becomes clouds and then rain?

options.text: Water vapour cools high in the air, condenses into tiny liquid droplets that form clouds, and those droplets may later join and fall as rain, hail, or snow.
Clouds are thick patches of water vapour that have not yet turned into liquid droplets.
As soon as tiny cloud droplets form, every cloud must start raining at once.
A cloud begins to rain only because it looks dark from the ground.

teacher.key_rationale: Water vapour cools and condenses into liquid droplets that make clouds; rain needs droplets to grow and fall. Clouds are not pure vapour; formation alone does not force rain; darkness is not the cause.
